metadata.topic: Pressure in Fluids — Shipwreck Depth, Total Pressure, and Force
metadata.caribbean_note: Context: shipwreck fully submerged at the bottom of the Caribbean Sea — authentic Caribbean marine setting linking to CSEC Q2a pressure concepts

question.name: CSEC Phy Jan 2023 Q2b — Shipwreck: Depth, Total Pressure, Hatch Force
question.text:
Figure 2 shows a shipwreck fully submerged at the bottom of the Caribbean Sea.

  • Liquid pressure on the top surface of the shipwreck: 430 kPa
  • Atmospheric pressure: 100 kPa
  • Density of sea water: ρ = 1 025 kg m⁻³
  • g = 10 N kg⁻¹
  • Area of hatch door on top surface: A = 0.60 m²
question.general_feedback:
(i) Depth: P_liquid = ρgh → h = P/(ρg) = 430 000 / (1 025 × 10) = 430 000 / 10 250 = 41.95 m ≈ 42 m

(ii) Total pressure: P_total = P_liquid + P_atm = 430 + 100 = 530 kPa

(iii) Force on hatch: F = P_total × A = 530 000 × 0.60 = 318 000 N

steps.label:
Given: P_liquid = 430 kPa  |  P_atm = 100 kPa  |  ρ = 1 025 kg m⁻³  |  g = 10 N kg⁻¹  |  A = 0.60 m²
Formulas: P_liquid = ρgh    P_total = P_liquid + P_atm    F = P × A
Part (i) — Calculate the depth of the shipwreck below the surface. (4 marks)
Part (ii) — Calculate the total pressure on the top surface of the shipwreck. (1 mark)
Part (iii) — Calculate the downward force on the hatch door due to total pressure. (3 marks)

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: Convert kPa to Pa: multiply by 1000. 430 kPa × 1000 = 430 000 Pa.

error_codes.SC_FORMULA_SELECTION_ERROR: Rearrange P_liquid = ρgh to get h = P/(ρg). Use P in Pa and ρg = 10 250.

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: Total pressure = liquid pressure + atmospheric pressure = 430 + 100 = 530 kPa.
error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Don't forget to add atmospheric pressure. At depth, total pressure = gauge (liquid) pressure + atmospheric pressure.

error_codes.SC_FORMULA_SELECTION_ERROR: Force = Pressure × Area. Use P = 530 000 Pa (total, not just liquid) and A = 0.60 m².
